title: The Simpsons Season 38: Children's Books, Chimps, and Horror Cups
summary:
What if your favorite children's books suddenly turned into Simpsons characters? That's exactly what happens in the Season 38 premiere of The Simpsons, airing September 27, 2026.

The episode is called "The Children's Book Job." Emma Thompson guest-stars as Constance Clavinger, a famous children's book author who comes to Springfield to save the elementary school. But she's a handful — she gets drunk at the airport bar! Homer has to drag her across town to a book fair organized by Marge.

In one scene, Homer daydreams that Springfield turns into kids' books like The Very Hungry Caterpillar, Captain Underpants, and Diary of a Wimpy Kid. Executive producer Matt Selman calls the episode a "love letter" to children's books.

Colin Jost also appears as himself, reading his own children's book to the kids — who look totally bored.

More episodes are coming. In "Diary of a Chimpy Kid," Bart and Lisa adopt a baby chimp. And "Treehouse of Horror XXXVII" has a Nightmare Before Christmas opening and a segment where Homer keeps turning into different husbands for Marge.

There's even a Jack in the Box meal with glow-in-the-dark cups. They sold out instantly — and now they're on eBay for $200!
why_it_matters: The Simpsons shows kids that jokes and stories can be built by playing with things you already know, like your favourite books.

background_read: The Simpsons is a cartoon about a funny family living in the make-believe town of Springfield; it first appeared on TV in 1989 and is one of the longest-running shows in America.
Every year the show makes a special spooky episode called 'Treehouse of Horror' around Halloween, which is on October 31.
Emma Thompson is an award-winning British actress, and Colin Jost is a comedian from the late-night TV show Saturday Night Live.
Article_Structure: WHO: The Simpsons family — Homer, Marge, Bart and Lisa — plus guest stars Emma Thompson and Colin Jost.
WHAT: The Season 38 premiere, 'The Children's Book Job', makes fun of children's books and brings a wild, tipsy author to town.
WHERE: Springfield, the make-believe town where the Simpsons live.
WHY: The show keeps going by spoofing real things kids know — picture books, horror films, and even fast-food toy cups.

perspectives.description: Long-time fans are happy the show still makes new episodes and love seeing parodies of books they grew up with.
Some people think a show that has run for so many seasons may slowly be running out of fresh ideas.
Collectors rushed to buy the Jack in the Box meal cups, and now the cups are being resold online for a lot of money.
